content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge is resolving a link where the challenger's pressed verses are being weighed as an own-chain collision, so K-C governs how the collision must be weighed.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8)","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"The phrase 'weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse' could mean the judge must expressly analyze the competing chains by footing, or merely that it must not decide by whether a single verse states the contrary; the text treats individual verses/word-counts as the weighing.","why":"The judge labels the link underdetermined by balancing individual verses and a word-count rather than weighing the competing chains by footing as K-C requires."}
